samples.summary: CodeRabbit latency cells take `n` from the wrong object (`self_timed.n` / `push_proxy.n` rather than the series' own `ms.n`), which mislabels the denominator or throws
samples.evidence: `latency: series(selfTimed?.ms) ? figure(selfTimed.ms, selfTimed.n, …)` — the guard is on `selfTimed.ms.n > 0` but the cell's `n` is the sibling `selfTimed.n`. Same at 715 for `pushProxy`. The panel path one block above correctly uses the series' own `wall.n` (684-685). If a payload's top-level `n` counts items while `ms.n` counts poolable measurements (the adapter distinguishes `measured` from `poolable`, coderabbit.mjs:1000, 1023-1032; the push-proxy fixture itself has `ms.n = 5`, `n_items = 7`), the figure is captioned with a denominator it was not measured at — the decision-33 failure the code claims to prevent. If `self_timed.n` is simply absent, `figure` refuses (report.mjs:201) and the whole render aborts even though the series is present.

verdict.reason: The payload-shape mismatch is real and verified in the tree. report.mjs:663/683/685/687 read panel.review_wall_ms, panel.review_cost_usd and panel.latency_interval, and :665-666/:711/:719 read coderabbit.latency.self_timed/push_proxy/triggers. The only producer, cost-latency.mjs, emits SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 (:75) with panel = {unit, replicates, per_item, by_size_bucket, replicate_spend_usd, duration_source} (:666-680) and coderabbit.latency = {wall_ms: null, reason} unconditionally (:684); per-review cost/wall exist only per replicate (:407-421), per item (:455-456) and per bucket (:493-494). No schema-2 producer exists anywhere (grep for review_cost_usd/latency_interval hits only report.mjs, report.test.mjs, the adapter's own latency spans, and docs). Consequences: against the only payload this repo can produce, §4's cost-per-review, wall-clock and CodeRabbit latency cells all fall to not-computed, and renderLatencyLimit (report.mjs:1415-1418) is unreachable because s.coderabbit.latency.availability can never be "present"; the assumed shape is exercised only by the schema_version: 2 fixture (report.test.mjs:124-155), so no test flags it, while the change's notes claim these figures render end to end (docs/.../20260812-eval-report-renderer-todo.md:459-461). The reviewer slightly overstates one detail — the pooled n=21 series is not in the payload under another key, so the not-computed wording is literally truthful for a schema-1 payload and report.mjs:634-638 documents that degradation — but that mitigation does not make the contract match any producer, and I found no version gate or caller-side guard that would refute the finding on a named ground.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end. report.mjs:761 gates the `suppressed` state on `Number.isFinite(fit.min_n)`, but the producer of that object, `fitCostToSize` (cost-latency.mjs:251-264), emits `{n, intercept_usd, slope_usd_per_1000_lines, fixed_share, reason}` with no `min_n` on either refusal branch, and cost-latency.mjs:422 feeds that return value verbatim into `cost_vs_size` on each entry of `panel.replicates` (built at 601/668), which is exactly what report.mjs:697-700 passes to `fitCell`. A repo-wide grep shows `min_n` on a `cost_vs_size` object only in test fixtures (report.test.mjs:135-137, 578, 605) and `MIN_FIT_ITEMS` only in prose comments — the constant does not exist. So on any real replicate with fewer than 3 priced items (reachable whenever items error out), the guard is dead and the cell renders through renderCell (report.mjs:261-262) as `**not measurable**`, which this module's own vocabulary (report.mjs:173-181) defines as 'cannot exist however long anyone runs it' — false for a fit a fourth item would produce, and precisely the state conflation report.mjs:183-184 calls a scoring bug. No guard or normaliser elsewhere injects `min_n`. Real, reachable, wrong output labeling: a correctness (wrong condition / unreachable branch) defect, major impact.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: report.mjs:711-715 guards on the series (`series(selfTimed?.ms)` / `series(pushProxy?.ms)`, where `series` at line 654 reads `s.n`, i.e. `ms.n`) but passes the sibling `selfTimed.n` / `pushProxy.n` as the figure's denominator. The sibling path one block up does it correctly (`wall = series(panel.review_wall_ms)`; `figure(wall, wall.n, …)` at 663/684-685), as does `seriesCell` at 661, and the module's own comment at 656-660 declares the violated invariant ("The `n` on the cell is the series' own"). Both consequences are reachable: (a) `figure` throws via `refuse` on a non-finite `n` (200-203) and `costLatencyFigures` is called unwrapped from `buildReport` (866), so a payload with `ms` present but no top-level `n` aborts the entire render — contrary to the documented "renders rather than throws for older payloads" contract at 634-638; (b) nothing pins `span.n === span.ms.n` — `validateScore` (store.mjs:383) checks only scorer id/scope, and no in-repo producer emits this shape (cost-latency.mjs:684 still emits `latency: {wall_ms: null, reason}`), so the only instance is the fixture at report.test.mjs:152-153 which itself carries four different counts on one span (`ms.n: 5`, `n: 5`, `n_items: 7`, `n_measured: 7`). No guard, caller, or validator makes either path unreachable, and the defect is squarely in the correctness lane (wrong value / crash on a data-shape-dependent path), so I have no named ground to refute.
